Name: Set up repo layout
Description: Create the top-level structure: apps/ (service code), infra/ (Terraform), k8s/ (manifests), argocd/, .github/workflows/. Agree naming so pipelines can filter on paths.
Acceptance Criteria: Folders exist with a short README each; layout documented in the root README.

Name: Catalogue the nine services
Description: Read the source of every service and record language, port, endpoints, env vars, secrets, tables touched and which services call which. This feeds every later card.
Acceptance Criteria: A service catalogue table in docs/ covers all nine services, including which ones publish or consume events.

Name: Run the stack locally with docker compose
Description: Run docker compose up --build and walk the order flow end to end locally to get a baseline before changing anything.
Acceptance Criteria: Order flow works locally: create order, reserve inventory, pay, ship, deliver. Any failures logged as bug cards.

Name: Set up Azure subscription access and a budget alert
Description: Confirm the subscription, register resource providers (ContainerService, KeyVault, ServiceBus and so on), check vCPU quota for three zones and create a budget with email alerts.
Acceptance Criteria: Providers registered, quota is enough for system plus user pools, budget alert fires to your inbox.

Name: Decide: event bus (Service Bus vs Strimzi vs Event Hubs)
Description: Compare Azure Service Bus, Strimzi Kafka in-cluster and Event Hubs Kafka endpoint on cost, ops burden, DLQ support and client changes. Later cards assume Service Bus; revisit them if you pick otherwise.
Acceptance Criteria: Short ADR written with the choice and trade-offs.

Name: Decide: Kustomize vs Helm
Description: Pick the manifest tooling for the nine services and platform components. Later cards assume Kustomize base plus overlays.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR written; README Architecture section can quote it.

Name: Decide: in-cluster Postgres vs Flexible Server rationale
Description: The brief mandates a StatefulSet. Write down why that is acceptable here and what you would pick for a real production team.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR covers cost, HA, backups, ops burden and zone behaviour.

Name: Decide: autoscaling approach (HPA vs KEDA)
Description: Decide which services scale on CPU/memory with HPA and which scale on queue depth with KEDA (the worker is the likely KEDA candidate).
Acceptance Criteria: ADR lists each service with its scaler, metric and min/max replicas.

Name: Decide: observability stack
Description: Compare New Relic, kube-prometheus-stack and Azure Managed Prometheus plus Managed Grafana on cost at this scale, ingest pricing, retention, ops burden and lock-in.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR with a cost table and a recommendation; reused in P10-07.

Name: Decide: secrets delivery (ESO vs Secrets Store CSI)
Description: Pick External Secrets Operator or the AKS azure-keyvault-secrets-provider add-on. Consider rotation behaviour and whether pods need restarts.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR written with the rotation story for each option.

Name: Swap SQS client for Service Bus SDK in order-service
Description: Replace the AWS SQS publisher with the Azure Service Bus SDK, authenticating with DefaultAzureCredential so Workload ID works in cluster.
Acceptance Criteria: Order events land on the Service Bus queue locally or in a dev namespace; no AWS SDK left in the service.

Name: Swap SQS client for Service Bus SDK in inventory-service
Description: Same change as P1-01 for inventory events.
Acceptance Criteria: Inventory events land on Service Bus; no AWS SDK left.

Name: Swap SQS client for Service Bus SDK in payment-service
Description: Same change as P1-01 for payment events.
Acceptance Criteria: Payment events land on Service Bus; no AWS SDK left.

Name: Swap SQS client for Service Bus SDK in shipping-service
Description: Same change as P1-01 for shipping events. Check P0-02 in case a different service is the fourth producer.
Acceptance Criteria: Shipping events land on Service Bus; no AWS SDK left.

Name: Swap SQS consumer for Service Bus receiver in worker
Description: Replace the SQS poll loop with a Service Bus receiver. Complete on success, abandon on failure so max_delivery_count moves poison messages to the DLQ.
Acceptance Criteria: Worker processes events end to end; a forced failure ends up in the dead-letter queue after the configured retries.

Name: Add health and readiness endpoints where missing
Description: Every service needs a liveness endpoint and a readiness endpoint that checks its real dependencies (DB, Redis, Service Bus).
Acceptance Criteria: All nine services expose both endpoints and return non-200 when a dependency is down.

Name: Make all config come from environment variables
Description: Remove any hardcoded hosts, credentials or keys. Everything configurable must come from env or mounted files so Key Vault can supply it.
Acceptance Criteria: grep for secrets and hostnames finds nothing hardcoded; services start from env alone.

Name: Handle graceful shutdown (SIGTERM)
Description: Services should stop accepting traffic, finish in-flight requests and close consumers on SIGTERM. Needed for zero-downtime rollouts and spot eviction.
Acceptance Criteria: Rolling a pod under load produces no 5xx; worker does not lose in-flight messages.

Name: Fix and PR real bugs found in the services
Description: For each real bug found, open a PR against the upstream repo with screenshots of the bug, the fix and the scenario working afterwards.
Acceptance Criteria: Each bug has a PR with before and after evidence.

Name: Update docker compose for the new messaging path
Description: Local dev still has to work after the SDK swap. Use the Service Bus emulator container or a dev namespace connection string for local only.
Acceptance Criteria: docker compose up runs the full flow with the new messaging clients.

Name: Write multi-stage Dockerfiles for Go services
Description: Build stage compiles a static binary; runtime stage is distroless or scratch. Pin base image digests.
Acceptance Criteria: Every Go service builds; runtime images are small and contain no build toolchain.

Name: Write multi-stage Dockerfiles for the remaining services
Description: Cover any non-Go services (for example dashboard-api with its UI build) with the same pattern: build stage, slim runtime stage.
Acceptance Criteria: All nine services have a Dockerfile and build cleanly.

Name: Harden images: non-root user and .dockerignore
Description: Run as a non-root UID, set a read-only-friendly filesystem layout, add .dockerignore files so secrets and build junk stay out of the context.
Acceptance Criteria: docker inspect shows a non-root user for every image; no .env or .git in any image.

Name: Scan images locally with Trivy
Description: Run Trivy against each image and fix or document HIGH and CRITICAL findings before the pipeline gate is added.
Acceptance Criteria: No unaddressed HIGH or CRITICAL vulnerabilities; exceptions listed with reasons.

Name: Point docker compose at the new Dockerfiles
Description: Make compose build from the new Dockerfiles so local dev matches what ships.
Acceptance Criteria: docker compose up --build runs the full order flow on the new images.

Name: Bootstrap Terraform remote state storage
Description: Create the state storage account and container (a small bootstrap root or script), with versioning, soft delete and no public blob access. The azurerm backend uses blob leases for locking.
Acceptance Criteria: terraform init uses the azurerm backend; a second concurrent plan is blocked by the lease.

Name: Structure Terraform roots and modules
Description: Split into sensible roots (for example platform and app-identity) and modules for network, aks, acr, servicebus, keyvault, dns. Pin provider versions.
Acceptance Criteria: terraform fmt and validate pass; each root has its own state key.

Name: Create resource groups and tagging
Description: Resource groups for platform, network and state, with consistent tags (project, env, owner) for cost tracking.
Acceptance Criteria: Plan and apply succeed; tags visible in Cost Management.

Name: Build VNet, private subnets and NSGs
Description: VNet with subnets for AKS nodes, private endpoints and the load balancer. Azure CNI Overlay needs no pod subnet. Keep NSG rules least-privilege.
Acceptance Criteria: Subnets exist with no public IPs on nodes; address plan documented.

Name: Design egress without a NAT Gateway
Description: Choose between the Standard LB outbound rules (default loadBalancer outbound type) and other options. Record the SNAT port limits and cost trade-off.
Acceptance Criteria: Outbound type set in Terraform; reasoning captured in README.

Name: Create private DNS zones for private endpoints
Description: Private DNS zones for ACR, Key Vault, Service Bus and blob, linked to the VNet.
Acceptance Criteria: Names resolve to private IPs from inside the VNet.

Name: Provision AKS cluster
Description: Latest GA AKS (1.33 or above), system pool across zones 1-3, OIDC issuer and Workload Identity enabled, Azure CNI Overlay, Entra ID auth with local accounts disabled.
Acceptance Criteria: kubectl get nodes shows system nodes in all three zones; OIDC issuer URL output from Terraform.

Name: Enable Node Auto Provisioning (NAP)
Description: Turn on NAP (Karpenter-based) for user workloads and define NodePools spread across three zones, including a spot pool for eviction-tolerant workloads.
Acceptance Criteria: Scaling a test deployment adds nodes via NAP in multiple zones; nodes scale back down when idle.

Name: Enable AKS add-ons
Description: Enable Azure Disk CSI (on by default, confirm), snapshot controller, and the Key Vault secrets provider add-on if P0-10 chose CSI.
Acceptance Criteria: Add-on pods running in kube-system.

Name: Create ACR with one repository per service
Description: Premium SKU (needed for private endpoints), admin user disabled. Repositories are created on first push; document the nine names.
Acceptance Criteria: ACR reachable only via private endpoint plus the CI path; admin user off.

Name: Grant AKS kubelet identity AcrPull
Description: Role assignment of AcrPull for the kubelet managed identity on the registry. Nothing broader.
Acceptance Criteria: A pod pulls an image from ACR with no imagePullSecret.

Name: Create Service Bus namespace and queue with dead-lettering
Description: Premium tier is needed for private endpoints. Queue with max_delivery_count (for example 3), dead-lettering on expiry, sensible lock duration.
Acceptance Criteria: Queue exists; a message abandoned three times appears in the DLQ.

Name: Create Key Vault and seed secrets
Description: RBAC authorisation mode, purge protection, soft delete. Generate DB password, JWT secret and API keys with random_password and store them, or seed out of band so values never sit in state in plaintext.
Acceptance Criteria: All secrets the services need exist in Key Vault; none in the repo or tfvars.

Name: Add private endpoints for ACR, Key Vault, Service Bus and state storage
Description: Private endpoints in the endpoint subnet, public network access disabled or restricted on each resource.
Acceptance Criteria: Each resource resolves privately from the cluster; public access blocked (CI access path documented).

Name: Create Azure DNS zone and delegate the domain
Description: Public DNS zone for the real domain; update registrar NS records.
Acceptance Criteria: dig NS returns Azure name servers.

Name: Create a managed identity per Azure-touching service
Description: One user-assigned managed identity per service that talks to Azure, with a federated credential bound to its namespace and ServiceAccount.
Acceptance Criteria: Identities and federated credentials exist; subjects match the planned ServiceAccounts.

Name: Assign least-privilege roles to service identities
Description: Scope roles to the minimum: Service Bus Data Sender for producers, Data Receiver for the worker, Key Vault Secrets User on specific secrets or the vault.
Acceptance Criteria: Role matrix in docs matches Terraform; no Contributor or Owner on workloads.

Name: Create identities for platform components
Description: Workload identities for ExternalDNS (DNS Zone Contributor on the zone), cert-manager (DNS-01 if used) and ESO (Key Vault Secrets User).
Acceptance Criteria: Each platform component authenticates without secrets.

Name: Set up Log Analytics and diagnostic settings
Description: Workspace plus AKS control plane diagnostics. Pick only the log categories you need and consider the Basic logs tier to control cost.
Acceptance Criteria: Control plane logs visible; expected monthly ingest estimated.

Name: Configure disk encryption
Description: Platform-managed keys are the default. Decide whether to add a Disk Encryption Set with a customer-managed key in Key Vault.
Acceptance Criteria: Choice recorded; if CMK, the DES exists and the StorageClass references it.

Name: Create GitHub Actions OIDC identity in Entra ID
Description: App registration or UAMI with federated credentials for the repo (branch main, pull_request, environments). Separate identities for infra and app pipelines with scoped roles.
Acceptance Criteria: A workflow logs in with azure/login and OIDC; no client secret exists anywhere.

Name: Create default Premium SSD StorageClass
Description: Azure Disk CSI StorageClass with Premium_ZRS, WaitForFirstConsumer, allowVolumeExpansion, marked default. Remove the default flag from the built-in class.
Acceptance Criteria: kubectl get sc shows only this class as default.

Name: Create VolumeSnapshotClass
Description: Snapshot class for disk.csi.azure.com, incremental snapshots.
Acceptance Criteria: A test VolumeSnapshot reaches readyToUse true.

Name: Install Traefik behind an Azure Standard Load Balancer
Description: Install Traefik via Helm (managed by ArgoCD later). Service type LoadBalancer with a static public IP and health probe annotations.
Acceptance Criteria: Traefik reachable on the public IP; dashboard not exposed publicly.

Name: Install cert-manager with a Let's Encrypt ClusterIssuer
Description: Staging and production ClusterIssuers. HTTP-01 through Traefik or DNS-01 through Azure DNS with Workload ID.
Acceptance Criteria: A test Certificate is issued by Let's Encrypt production.

Name: Install ExternalDNS for Azure DNS
Description: Workload ID auth, domain filter on your zone, TXT registry so it only touches records it owns.
Acceptance Criteria: Creating an Ingress creates the A record automatically.

Name: Install External Secrets Operator and a ClusterSecretStore
Description: ESO with a ClusterSecretStore pointing at Key Vault via Workload ID. Skip if P0-10 chose the CSI driver and do a SecretProviderClass instead.
Acceptance Criteria: A test ExternalSecret syncs a Key Vault value into a Kubernetes Secret.

Name: Create namespaces, quotas and pod security
Description: Namespaces for platform, data and apps. Pod Security Admission at restricted where possible, ResourceQuotas and LimitRanges.
Acceptance Criteria: Privileged pods rejected in app namespaces.

Name: Deploy PostgreSQL StatefulSet
Description: Single-replica StatefulSet with a 20Gi volumeClaimTemplate on the Premium SSD class, credentials from Key Vault, probes, resource requests, pinned image.
Acceptance Criteria: Postgres Ready; data survives a pod delete.

Name: Deploy Redis StatefulSet with AOF
Description: Redis with appendonly yes on a 10Gi PVC, password from Key Vault, probes and a pinned image.
Acceptance Criteria: Keys survive a pod delete; AOF file present on the volume.

Name: Keep stateful pods off spot and spread safely
Description: Node affinity to on-demand nodes, PDB to block voluntary eviction, priority class. Record what happens to a ZRS vs LRS disk when the pod moves zone.
Acceptance Criteria: Stateful pods never land on spot; zone behaviour documented.

Name: Design the database migration strategy
Description: Seven services share one database. Pick Job, init container or pre-sync hook, a migration tool, and an expand/contract pattern for rollback.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR written; covers the add-a-column scenario from the brief.

Name: Implement the migration Job
Description: Migration Job run as an ArgoCD PreSync hook (or equivalent) before app rollouts, idempotent and locked so two runs cannot collide.
Acceptance Criteria: A new migration applies once on sync; failure blocks the app rollout.

Name: Take a volume snapshot and restore it
Description: Snapshot the Postgres PVC, create a new PVC from it, start Postgres on the restored volume and check the data.
Acceptance Criteria: Restored database contains the rows written before the snapshot; steps recorded as a runbook.

Name: Schedule regular disk snapshots
Description: CronJob creating VolumeSnapshots with retention, or Azure Backup for AKS.
Acceptance Criteria: Snapshots appear on schedule and old ones are pruned.

Name: Create Kustomize base per service
Description: Deployment, Service and ServiceAccount per service. Probes, requests and limits, securityContext non-root and read-only root filesystem.
Acceptance Criteria: kustomize build renders valid manifests for all nine services.

Name: Create the dev overlay
Description: Overlay with image tags, replica counts and env-specific config. This is where CI bumps image tags.
Acceptance Criteria: kustomize build overlays/dev renders all services with dev settings.

Name: Configure zero-downtime rolling updates
Description: RollingUpdate maxUnavailable 0 and maxSurge 1, readiness gates traffic, preStop sleep, progressDeadlineSeconds so a bad rollout fails fast.
Acceptance Criteria: A rollout under load produces no errors; a broken image fails the rollout instead of taking traffic.

Name: Add PodDisruptionBudgets and topology spread
Description: PDBs for every multi-replica service; topologySpreadConstraints across zones.
Acceptance Criteria: Draining a node never drops a service to zero ready pods.

Name: Wire ServiceAccounts to Workload Identity
Description: Annotate ServiceAccounts with the client ID of each managed identity and label pods azure.workload.identity/use.
Acceptance Criteria: Each service reaches Service Bus or Key Vault with its own identity and nothing else.

Name: Create ExternalSecrets per service
Description: One ExternalSecret per service, pulling only the keys it needs. Add Reloader (or checksum annotations) so rotation rolls only affected pods.
Acceptance Criteria: No Secret manifests in git; rotating one key restarts only the services that use it.

Name: Create Ingress with TLS and path routing
Description: Single Ingress (or Traefik IngressRoute) for the domain, TLS from cert-manager, routes to api-gateway and dashboard-api as the code requires.
Acceptance Criteria: https://<domain> serves the dashboard with a valid certificate; API paths hit the gateway.

Name: Add NetworkPolicies
Description: Default deny per namespace, then allow only the calls in the service catalogue (for example only services that need it can reach Postgres).
Acceptance Criteria: A pod without an allow rule cannot reach Postgres or other services.

Name: Configure autoscaling per service
Description: HPA on CPU for the HTTP services, KEDA on Service Bus queue length for the worker, fixed replicas for scheduler and stateful sets.
Acceptance Criteria: Load test triggers scale-out; worker scales with queue depth.

Name: Place eviction-tolerant workloads on spot
Description: Tolerations and affinity for stateless services that survive eviction. Keep payment, scheduler and stateful pods on on-demand nodes.
Acceptance Criteria: Spot eviction of a node causes no failed orders.

Name: Deploy the scheduler as CronJobs or a Deployment
Description: Decide from the code whether scheduler runs as a long-lived process or Kubernetes CronJobs. Ensure only one instance runs a job at a time.
Acceptance Criteria: Expired reservations and abandoned orders are cleaned up on schedule with no duplicate runs.

Name: Install ArgoCD
Description: Install via Helm or manifests, admin via Entra SSO or at least a rotated admin password, UI not exposed publicly without auth.
Acceptance Criteria: ArgoCD UI reachable securely; repo connected.

Name: Create the App-of-Apps root Application
Description: Root Application pointing at argocd/apps, which holds child Applications for platform components, data layer and each service.
Acceptance Criteria: Syncing the root creates every child Application.

Name: Move platform components under ArgoCD
Description: Traefik, cert-manager, ExternalDNS, ESO, StorageClass and snapshot class all managed as ArgoCD Applications.
Acceptance Criteria: Deleting a platform resource by hand gets it recreated by ArgoCD.

Name: Order syncs with sync waves
Description: Waves: CRDs and platform first, then data layer, then migrations, then services.
Acceptance Criteria: A fresh cluster bootstraps from the root app in the right order without manual steps.

Name: Enable auto-sync on the dev overlay
Description: Automated sync with prune and self-heal for dev.
Acceptance Criteria: A merged tag bump deploys without anyone clicking sync.

Name: Define the rollback path for a single service
Description: Git revert of the tag bump as the standard rollback; note how auto-sync interacts with argocd app rollback. Keep each service a separate Application so one rollback does not touch the other eight.
Acceptance Criteria: Runbook written and exercised in P9-05.

Name: Build the infra pipeline
Description: GitHub Actions on infra/** only: fmt, validate, tflint, plan on PR with the plan posted as a comment; apply on merge to main behind an environment approval.
Acceptance Criteria: A PR touching infra shows a plan; merging applies it; app-only PRs do not trigger it.

Name: Build the app pipeline with change detection
Description: Workflow on apps/** with a per-service matrix from a path filter so only changed services build.
Acceptance Criteria: Changing one service builds only that service.

Name: Add image scanning gate
Description: Trivy scan in CI fails the job on HIGH or CRITICAL before the image is pushed. Upload SARIF to GitHub code scanning.
Acceptance Criteria: A vulnerable test image fails the pipeline and never reaches ACR.

Name: Push images to ACR with immutable tags
Description: Log in to ACR via OIDC, tag with the commit SHA, never reuse tags.
Acceptance Criteria: Images in ACR tagged by SHA; no latest tag used in manifests.

Name: Bump image tags in the dev overlay
Description: After a successful push, update the overlay image tag (kustomize edit set image) and commit or open a PR, which ArgoCD then syncs.
Acceptance Criteria: Push to payment-service ends with only payment-service redeployed.

Name: Validate manifests in CI
Description: kustomize build plus kubeconform (and optionally kube-linter or Checkov) on PRs touching k8s/.
Acceptance Criteria: An invalid manifest fails the PR check.

Name: Protect main and set up environments
Description: Branch protection with required checks, GitHub environments for apply with reviewers, OIDC subjects bound to those environments.
Acceptance Criteria: Direct pushes to main blocked; apply needs approval.

Name: Confirm all nine services healthy on AKS
Description: All Deployments available, no crash loops, readiness green.
Acceptance Criteria: kubectl get pods shows all nine services Ready; ArgoCD all Synced and Healthy.

Name: Run the end-to-end flow through the dashboard
Description: Create order, reserve inventory, process payment, ship, deliver, all from the dashboard over HTTPS at the real DNS name.
Acceptance Criteria: Order reaches delivered; screenshots or recording captured.

Name: Prove persistence across pod restarts
Description: Delete the Postgres and Redis pods and confirm data survives.
Acceptance Criteria: Orders and cache keys still present after restart.

Name: Test a zero-downtime rollout under load
Description: Run a load generator (k6 or hey) while deploying a new version of a service.
Acceptance Criteria: Zero failed requests during the rollout.

Name: Drill: roll back a bad image
Description: Push a broken notification-service image, watch the rollout fail, roll back via git revert. Time it.
Acceptance Criteria: Other eight services unaffected; rollback time recorded.

Name: Test dead-lettering after repeated failures
Description: Send a poison event and confirm it lands in the DLQ after max_delivery_count. Decide how DLQ messages get inspected and replayed.
Acceptance Criteria: Poison message in DLQ; replay procedure documented.

Name: Test payment-service outage behaviour
Description: Scale payment-service to zero for two minutes mid-flow and see what happens to in-flight orders.
Acceptance Criteria: Orders resume or fail with a clear status once payment is back; behaviour documented.

Name: Test secret rotation
Description: Rotate the database password in Key Vault and Postgres, watch it propagate. Note which deployments restart.
Acceptance Criteria: Services recover with the new password; restart scope matches the design.

Name: Test zone failure and pod rescheduling
Description: Cordon and drain nodes in one zone and watch Postgres move. Confirm ZRS disk attaches in another zone.
Acceptance Criteria: Postgres comes back in a different zone with its data.

Name: Audit for hardcoded secrets and long-lived credentials
Description: Run gitleaks over the repo history, confirm no client secrets on any app registration, no storage keys in pipelines.
Acceptance Criteria: gitleaks clean; no credentials with an expiry exist for CI or workloads.

Name: Confirm the pipeline deploys only what changed
Description: Make a one-line change to payment-service and follow it through CI and ArgoCD.
Acceptance Criteria: Only payment-service builds and redeploys; captured for the README walkthrough.

Name: Write README: architecture decisions
Description: What was built, why, and what was traded off. Include StatefulSet vs Flexible Server and Kustomize vs Helm.
Acceptance Criteria: Section links to the ADRs and makes real decisions, not filler.

Name: Write README: deployment pipeline walkthrough
Description: Commit to live traffic for a payment-service change; how infra and app changes stay apart; where ArgoCD fits.
Acceptance Criteria: A reader can follow the flow step by step.

Name: Write README: secrets management
Description: Key Vault to pod path and what happens on rotation.
Acceptance Criteria: Matches the tested behaviour from P9-08.

Name: Write README: storage and restore
Description: How the PVC is backed, encryption choice, snapshots, tested restore procedure.
Acceptance Criteria: Restore procedure copied from the tested runbook.

Name: Write README: scaling strategy
Description: Which services scale, on what metric, what stays fixed, what breaks first under load.
Acceptance Criteria: Backed by load test results.

Name: Write README: database migrations
Description: How schema changes are applied and rolled back, including the add-a-column scenario.
Acceptance Criteria: Section matches the implemented Job.

Name: Write README: observability stack comparison
Description: Cost at this scale, ingest pricing, retention, ops burden, lock-in, and the pick for a real team.
Acceptance Criteria: Includes a cost table with sources.

Name: Answer the Things to Consider questions
Description: Short answers to each scenario in the brief: zone moves, DLQ, payment outage, column changes, bad image, spot, logging cost, password rotation, single-zone disks.
Acceptance Criteria: Every question answered, with evidence from drills where available.

Name: Draw the architecture diagram
Description: One diagram showing network, cluster, data, messaging, CI/CD and GitOps flows.
Acceptance Criteria: Diagram embedded in the README.

Name: Prepare to explain every resource
Description: Walk the Terraform and manifests and make sure you can justify each resource. Delete anything you cannot explain.
Acceptance Criteria: Resource inventory list with a one-line reason each.

Name: Deploy the chosen observability stack
Description: Install New Relic, kube-prometheus-stack or Managed Prometheus plus Grafana per the P0-09 decision.
Acceptance Criteria: Metrics from all nine services and the data layer visible.

Name: Build service-level dashboards (RED and saturation)
Description: RED metrics for the API layer, saturation for Postgres, Redis and Service Bus, grouped by service rather than pod.
Acceptance Criteria: Can answer which service, when it started, what changed and who is affected within 10 minutes without kubectl exec.

Name: Configure alerts routed to a human
Description: A small set of alerts that mean something (error rate, latency, DLQ depth, disk fill) routed to email, Slack or similar.
Acceptance Criteria: A test alert reaches the channel.

Name: Run an OpenTelemetry collector
Description: OTel collector in the cluster exporting via OTLP to Tempo, Jaeger or New Relic.
Acceptance Criteria: Collector receives and exports spans.

Name: Instrument the Go services with OTel
Description: Add the OTel SDK and propagate context across HTTP and Service Bus messages.
Acceptance Criteria: One order is traceable across api-gateway, order, payment, shipping and worker.

Name: Add a service mesh with mTLS
Description: AKS Istio add-on or Linkerd. Strict mTLS, authorisation policies to block lateral movement, traffic shifting for canaries.
Acceptance Criteria: Plaintext pod-to-pod calls rejected; a canary split works.

Name: Migrate from Ingress to Gateway API
Description: Replace the Ingress with GatewayClass, Gateway and HTTPRoute on Traefik.
Acceptance Criteria: Same routes and TLS served through Gateway API resources.

Name: Cluster backup and restore to a fresh cluster
Description: Velero with the Azure plugin or Azure Backup for AKS. Restore into a new cluster and prove the app comes back with its data.
Acceptance Criteria: Fresh cluster serves the dashboard with the original orders.

Name: Chaos drill: kill Postgres live
Description: Delete the Postgres pod during a demo and show the StatefulSet and the application recovering.
Acceptance Criteria: Recovery time recorded; no data loss.

Name: Tear down all infrastructure
Description: terraform destroy in reverse order of roots; keep the state storage until last.
Acceptance Criteria: Resource groups empty or deleted.

Name: Check for orphaned billable resources
Description: Look for leftover managed disks, snapshots, public IPs, load balancers, the node resource group and Log Analytics ingestion.
Acceptance Criteria: Cost Management shows spend dropping to zero the following day.
